# Delays are not observed exactly

## Two events, two windows

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}
![](../figures/delays-double-censoring.png){fig-alt="A timeline. A blue
box marks the primary event window of width w_P, a red box marks the
secondary event window of width w_S, an arrow between them is the
delay T, and a dashed line further right marks the observation cutoff
C, beyond which longer delays have not been seen."}

::: {.attribution}
Diagram drawn for this talk, `scripts/delays-double-censoring.py`
:::

$$
F_{\mathrm{pc}}(t) \;=\; \int_{0}^{w_P} F_{d}(t - u)\, f_{p}(u)\,
\mathrm{d}u
$$

$F_d$ is the delay CDF and $f_p$ the density of when, inside a primary
window of width $w_P$, the primary event happened.
:::
::: {.column width="46%"}
- A delay is the time between two events. Infection to symptom onset,
  onset to hospitalisation, onset to death
- Neither event is seen at a point in time. Both arrive as a day,
  sometimes a week
- Ignore any of that and the estimate is **biased**
:::
::::

## The pairs that have not finished yet are missing

![](../figures/delays-right-truncation.png){width="72%"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Two panels. On the left, the delay distribution seen by day 7
and by day 14 sits well to the left of the true distribution. On the
right, the mean estimated delay rises from under 2 days towards the
true mean of 5.9 days as the cutoff moves away from now, passing 3.9
days at a cutoff of 7 and 5.3 days at a cutoff of 14."}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- In real time you only see the pairs whose secondary event has already
  happened, and the shortfall grows the nearer the cutoff is to now
- **This is not censoring.** Censoring is not knowing *when* an event
  happened inside a window. Truncation is not seeing the pair *at all*
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```julia
d = primary_censored(LogNormal(μ, σ), Uniform(0, 1))
seen = interval_censored(truncated(d; upper = C), 1)
```

- Divide by the CDF at the cutoff. `truncated` is
  `Distributions.truncated`, which does not know what it is wrapping
- The delay estimate is an input elsewhere, so a mean of **3.9 days
  rather than 5.9** is what the forecast and the transmission model are
  handed
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
`LogNormal(1.6, 0.6)` with daily windows, computed for this talk with
`CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22,
`scripts/delays-right-truncation.jl`
:::
